title: Write an nginx Reverse Proxy with HTTPS from Scratch
intro: The tutorials read nginx configuration; now write one. This is the file most small production services sit behind: two app servers, HTTP redirected to HTTPS, the standard proxy headers, and static files served directly. Every nginx directive ends with a semicolon, and blocks use braces.

steps.prompt:
Write shop.conf with three top-level blocks:

(1) upstream backend: least_conn, and two servers, 10.0.1.11:8080 and 10.0.1.12:8080.

(2) A server for plain HTTP: listen 80, server_name shop.example.com, and
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;

(3) A server for HTTPS: listen 443 ssl, server_name shop.example.com,
    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/shop.example.com/fullchain.pem
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/shop.example.com/privkey.pem
    and two locations:
    - location / : proxy_pass http://backend; plus four proxy_set_header lines:
        Host $host
        X-Real-IP $remote_addr
        X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for
        X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme
    - location /static/ : root /var/www/shop; and expires 7d;
steps.fake_output:
nginx: the configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful
steps.explanation: A complete front door: two balanced app servers, HTTPS with a redirect from HTTP, the headers the app needs to know its real client, and static files that never touch the app.
steps.why: Each line prevents a problem from the tutorials. 'return 301 https://$host$request_uri' keeps the path and query string, where a hand-written rewrite often drops them. fullchain.pem, not cert.pem, includes the intermediate certificate that command-line clients and mobile apps need. 'proxy_pass http://backend' has no trailing slash, so /api/users reaches the app unchanged (webservers-tutorial-003). Without the Host and X-Forwarded headers the app sees every request as coming from nginx over plain HTTP, and builds wrong links and redirect loops. Serving /static/ from disk with a 7-day expiry takes that load off the app entirely. With 'root', /static/app.css is read from /var/www/shop/static/app.css. For production you'd add: an explicit default server that drops unknown hostnames (webservers-incident-004), ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3, HSTS, upstream keepalive, and timeouts. The next lab hardens a config like this one.
